items.label: f03-export-row-before-estimate
items.front: Why does exportsService.create estimate the row count BEFORE inserting the ExportJob row?
items.back: The estimate can throw on an invalid date window. Estimating second would leave an orphaned PENDING job behind every rejected request — rows nothing processes that inflate the queue-depth metric.

items.label: f02-say-what-not-verified
items.front: PR habit: what should the Verification section say besides the commands that passed, and why?
items.back: What you did NOT verify (e.g. the Playwright spec never ran locally; only CI ran it). A reviewer who knows the gap can weigh it; one told 'all tests pass' cannot.

items.label: f01-commit-body
items.front: In 3buildanalytics' git conventions, what three questions should a commit body answer?
items.back: What was the behaviour before, and why was it wrong? Why this fix and not an obvious alternative? What did you deliberately not do? The summary says what; the body says why.

items.prompt: metricVisibilityMiddleware tried to stop non-privileged users from forcing ?refresh=true by assigning to req.query. What actually happened?

choices.text: Everyone, admins included, was blocked from refreshing their dashboards
Express re-parses req.query, so the assignment was silently discarded
It worked, but just for requests that also sent a startDate parameter
It threw on every request, so each dashboard call returned a 500 error

choices: Everyone, admins included, was blocked from refreshing their dashboards
Express re-parses req.query, so the assignment was silently discarded
It worked, but just for requests that also sent a startDate parameter
It threw on every request, so each dashboard call returned a 500 error

items.explanation: US-16 opened by testing the control: 'It did not — Express re-parses req.query, so the assignment was discarded.' The proving commit is worth more than the fix. Any user could still force a full recomputation.

items.prompt: Why does this repo merge PRs with --merge rather than --squash?

choices.text: Its commits are reviewable chapters that squashing would collapse
Squash merges cannot delete the source branch afterwards
Squash merges break the required CI status checks on protected branches
--merge produces the linear history that git bisect requires

choices: Its commits are reviewable chapters that squashing would collapse
Squash merges cannot delete the source branch afterwards
Squash merges break the required CI status checks on protected branches
--merge produces the linear history that git bisect requires

items.explanation: 'Squashing would collapse those seven chapters into one blob and destroy exactly the thing this history exists to teach.' Squash is reasonable where commits are checkpoints.

items.prompt: Writing auth tests surfaced a malformed token returning 500, outside the PR's scope. How did the PR record it?

choices.text: It deleted the failing test until the follow-up story could start
A TODO comment over the auth middleware naming the follow-up story
A quiet fix in the same PR, since the change was only one line long
An it.skip test for the right behavior, plus a test pinning the 500

choices: It deleted the failing test until the follow-up story could start
A TODO comment over the auth middleware naming the follow-up story
A quiet fix in the same PR, since the change was only one line long
An it.skip test for the right behavior, plus a test pinning the 500

items.explanation: 'Encode the follow-up in the test suite, not in a TODO comment. TODOs rot silently; a failing assertion does not.' A fix then forces the skip to be revisited.

items.prompt: The cache client was wrapped in try/catch so Redis was 'optional'. Why did requests hang instead of degrading when Redis was down?

choices.text: Express does not run try/catch blocks inside async route handlers at all
With maxRetriesPerRequest null, ioredis queued commands and nothing threw
BullMQ held a lock on the shared Redis connection for the whole request
The catch block re-threw the error and crashed the request handler instead

choices: Express does not run try/catch blocks inside async route handlers at all
With maxRetriesPerRequest null, ioredis queued commands and nothing threw
BullMQ held a lock on the shared Redis connection for the whole request
The catch block re-threw the error and crashed the request handler instead

items.explanation: The fix(cache) commit explains that maxRetriesPerRequest: null made ioredis wait forever. Lesson: 'bound the operation yourself; do not trust a library's timeout defaults.'

items.prompt: A Viewer reports seeing a revenue metric they should not. Navigation already hides the revenue page for Viewers. Where should you look?

choices.text: Backend permission middleware and server-side metric filtering
Frontend route guards, which must be missing for the Viewer role
The seed data, since Viewers should never be given any revenue events
The cache TTL, since stale cached data leaks old permissions

choices: Backend permission middleware and server-side metric filtering
Frontend route guards, which must be missing for the Viewer role
The seed data, since Viewers should never be given any revenue events
The cache TTL, since stale cached data leaks old permissions

items.explanation: 'Role Sees Too Much: Verify backend permission middleware. Verify server-side metric visibility filtering. Do not trust frontend navigation hiding as security.' Hidden navigation is not security.

items.prompt: US-18's rate-limit tests were green in CI. What was really happening?

choices.text: A mock Redis let each request straight through, so no limit ever fired
They passed because the limiter got disabled in the CI environment file
They were marked it.skip on purpose and assigned to a later story
A cold lazyConnect client failed its first ping, so they skipped themselves

choices: A mock Redis let each request straight through, so no limit ever fired
They passed because the limiter got disabled in the CI environment file
They were marked it.skip on purpose and assigned to a later story
A cold lazyConnect client failed its first ping, so they skipped themselves

items.explanation: 'US-18's rate-limit tests reported green in CI while doing nothing, because a cold lazyConnect client failed its first ping(). Tests that skip quietly are worse than tests that fail.'

items.prompt: Why does the backend return KPI aggregates instead of raw event rows for the frontend to summarize?

choices.text: Raw rows are slower, leakier and harder to reason about
Redis can only cache scalar values, not arrays of rows
Raw rows would exceed the 10,000-row export limit
The frontend charting library cannot group raw rows by date

choices: Raw rows are slower, leakier and harder to reason about
Redis can only cache scalar values, not arrays of rows
Raw rows would exceed the 10,000-row export limit
The frontend charting library cannot group raw rows by date

items.explanation: 'Returning raw rows and asking the frontend to compute metrics is slower, leakier, and harder to reason about.' Leakier matters for role-based visibility.

items.prompt: US-12 passed on the laptop but failed in CI. What was the cause?

choices.text: CI ran the test files in parallel while the laptop ran them serially
CI's clock was in UTC, shifting the rollup's date window
resetDatabase() never cleared Redis, and the laptop had no Redis
The laptop used SQLite while CI ran against a real Postgres server

choices: CI ran the test files in parallel while the laptop ran them serially
CI's clock was in UTC, shifting the rollup's date window
resetDatabase() never cleared Redis, and the laptop had no Redis
The laptop used SQLite while CI ran against a real Postgres server

items.explanation: 'resetDatabase() truncated tables but never cleared Redis, and there is no Redis on the dev machine. An argument for CI running the real dependencies.'

items.prompt: An export is estimated at 50,000 rows and Redis is unreachable when it is dispatched. What happens?

choices.text: Queueing fails, a warning is logged, and it is processed synchronously
Nothing runs: the job stays PENDING until Redis returns and a worker takes it
It is processed synchronously, but only up to the 10,000-row limit
The request fails with 503 and the job row is deleted to avoid orphans

choices: Queueing fails, a warning is logged, and it is processed synchronously
Nothing runs: the job stays PENDING until Redis returns and a worker takes it
It is processed synchronously, but only up to the 10,000-row limit
The request fails with 503 and the job row is deleted to avoid orphans

items.explanation: dispatchJob runs processJob directly for <= MAX_SYNC_EXPORT_ROWS (10,000); above that it tries the queue and, on error, logs export.queue.unavailable.falling_back and processes synchronously.

items.prompt: The old export retry reset the job to PENDING and then called create(). Why did the engineering dashboard's backlog climb on every retry?

choices.text: The retry deleted completed jobs, so only pending ones remained
create() inserted a second job, leaving the original PENDING forever
Each retry doubled the estimated row count of the export job
Retries were counted twice by the BullMQ metrics exporter's gauge

choices: The retry deleted completed jobs, so only pending ones remained
create() inserted a second job, leaving the original PENDING forever
Each retry doubled the estimated row count of the export job
Retries were counted twice by the BullMQ metrics exporter's gauge

items.explanation: The retry comment explains the leak: every retry left 'one permanently-pending row'. Retry now reuses the same row and caps retries at MAX_RETRIES (3). Queue depth counts PENDING rows.

items.prompt: The side-effects guide warns that a retried export could re-emit tracked and audit events. What does processJob now do when BullMQ redelivers a job another worker already took?

choices.text: Processing runs again, but the second audit event row is suppressed
It throws a 409, which BullMQ then treats as a permanent job failure
Its conditional claim updates zero rows, so it returns the existing job
It waits for the other worker to finish, then writes a second CSV file

choices: Processing runs again, but the second audit event row is suppressed
It throws a 409, which BullMQ then treats as a permanent job failure
Its conditional claim updates zero rows, so it returns the existing job
It waits for the other worker to finish, then writes a second CSV file

items.explanation: Only PENDING or FAILED rows can be claimed (status set to PROCESSING atomically); 'if it touches zero rows someone else already has it, so we return their result rather than duplicating the work.' It logs already_claimed and does not reprocess.
